name: react-viewer
title: The bundle viewer becomes a TypeScript and React application, built at author time into one file
outcome: A reader opens the bundle on three goal-shaped surfaces instead of five record-type tabs, an engineer changes one surface by opening one typed React component, and the file that ships is still one self-contained HTML page that publishes as an Artifact unchanged.
done_when: the viewer opens on a Work board that lists every design with its stage, epic progress, and which records exist, and a lane filter narrows it to the work that needs a decision, a build, or a review

a design opens through six lenses (intent, problem and solution, architecture, risks and verdict, build, pull requests), and the intent lens leads with the intent prose and ends with the done-when list as bullet points
a lens with no record is disabled rather than empty, and a backlog design that carries only goal.json renders correctly, with its greyed lenses stated as the honest record state
the Flight deck is its own surface, and it shows a pull request's four narration levels, its Mermaid diagrams, its scene art, its intent and assessment, and the joins that reach it
plugins/artifact/viewer/index.html is produced by a Vite build from typed React sources under viewer/src/, and a test fails when the committed output does not equal a fresh build
npm install and npm run build run only when an engineer changes the viewer, never at /plugin install and never in the browser
export_artifact.py matches named markers the build emits on purpose, instead of incidental literals, and publishing a pull request still succeeds
the five record-type tabs are gone, and every record they showed is reachable from one of the three surfaces

the three items build-workflow-polish carried outside the viewer are delivered here: the design-to-implement handoff line, the slice-table column shape, and the missing commit step after an accepted slice
a review comment reaches feedback-ledger.jsonl when the viewer is served with --allow-write, and the viewer never claims a comment will sync when nothing syncs
a published Artifact marks comments read-only, collects them in the browser, and hands the reviewer one block to paste back into the ledger
abort_if: a byte-equal rebuild cannot be made reliable across machines, because a lockfile and a pinned Node version do not produce identical output, which would make the guard test flaky and the committed file untrustworthy
the built single file plus its inlined data exceeds the 16 MiB Artifact budget for a normal pull request, and dropping audio does not recover it
Claude Artifacts will not render a Mermaid block that React injects after page load, and a vendored Mermaid runtime pushes the published file over the same budget

min_work.derived_from: 6 districts, 5 colliding ADRs (0001, 0018, 0019, 0020, 0022), 1 bounded context (cobuilder-packaging), 1 boundary rule on the install surface, 4899 measured viewer lines, 1 working prototype built in this session

epics.outcome: export_artifact.py matches named markers, and a test proves a publish still works after the markers move
epics.note: The exporter rewrites the viewer by verbatim string replacement today and hard-errors when a literal moves. A bundled build moves every literal, so this seam must become explicit before any build lands.

epics.outcome: a publish spike answers the three platform unknowns, then npm run build produces the committed index.html and a test rebuilds it and fails on any difference
epics.note: Vite plus vite-plugin-singlefile, a lockfile, and a pinned Node version. This epic starts with a spike, at the engineer's direction: publish one throwaway bundled page and measure the byte-equal rebuild across two machines, the size with React inlined, and whether a Claude Artifact renders a Mermaid block that React injects after page load. Two of the three abort conditions are settled by that spike, before five epics of work depend on the answer.

epics.outcome: one typed model reads window.STORY, window.ODYSSEY, window.DIFFS, window.ADRS, window.DESIGNS, window.DIAGRAMS and index.json, and the joins are resolved in one place
epics.note: The viewer resolves joins by hand in each render path today. index.json already computed them. This epic makes the index the source and the types the contract.

epics.outcome: the Work board and the seven design lenses render every design, including a backlog design with goal.json only
epics.note: The prototype of 2026-09-07 is the reference for this surface.

epics.outcome: the Flight deck renders a pull request at parity with today's viewer, plus the joins rail
epics.note: Parity covers the four levels, diagrams, scene art, narration audio, the diff, and the intent and assessment sheet.

epics.outcome: decisions and map coverage move to a Reference surface, and the five record-type tabs are removed
epics.note: tests/test_viewer_modes.py asserts the five data-mode buttons. That test changes with this epic, and the change is the point, not a regression.

epics.outcome: a published Artifact of one pull request renders every surface, under the 16 MiB budget
epics.note: Closes the loop on E1. Measures the real budget with React inlined, and settles the Mermaid question the third abort condition names.

epics.outcome: the three non-viewer items from build-workflow-polish ship, so closing that design loses nothing
epics.note: build-workflow-polish is superseded by this design at the engineer's direction. Its E4, the tab-based viewer layout, is absorbed by E4 and E5 here. Its other three epics are not viewer work and would be lost silently: E1 adds the pointer from design mode stage 7 to /implement:start, E2 states the six-column slice-table shape that shared/slice_table.py parses, and E3 commits an accepted slice without a second prompt. They are carried here so the supersede is safe.

epics.outcome: the served viewer files a comment to the ledger or says plainly that it did not, and a published Artifact collects comments and hands them back as one pasteable block, with anchors that survive a React re-render
epics.note: The comment mechanism does not work today, and the engineer confirmed it on 2026-09-07. Three causes, all verified in the tree. First, LEDGER_AVAILABLE at viewer/index.html line 1399 tests only whether fetch exists in the browser, which is always true, so it never tells a reviewer that no ledger server is listening. Second, a failed POST falls back to localStorage and shows 'Will sync when server is reachable', although nothing syncs: no code reads that key back. Third, a published Artifact cannot reach any server, because the Artifact CSP blocks fetch, so every comment left where review actually happens is written to one browser's localStorage and lost. This epic also settles ADR-0019's anchoring under React, which owns the DOM the anchor walk uses. The transport is decided: the served viewer keeps POST /feedback under --allow-write, and the published Artifact marks comments read-only and exports them for paste-back through the copy-as-markdown path that already exists. The Artifact platform's own storage is rejected, because it would make the published page behave differently from the served one, which is the split ADR-0001 exists to prevent.
